thread:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: P1 ALERT — elevated latency observed on canary model 'redwood-1-canary' (95th = 3.2s, SLO 1.2s). Started ~09:13:50Z. No error-rate spike. Paging oncall.
Mia (oncall): taking pager — on it. Quick ask: is this affecting hosted API only or dedicated too?
Sam P.: hosted only so far, traffic routed to canary pool ~09:10Z. No rollback yet.
Lia Chen: adding timeline here, please drop logs and diffs in-thread.
Mia (oncall): initial triage — looks like token generation timeouts are not happening, just big tail latency on streaming chunk ack. Rolling a quick histogram from host metrics.
Mia (oncall): histogram: 50th=0.12s, 90th=0.55s, 95th=3.2s, 99th=6.1s. Request QPS stable.
AJ Rao: can we get model runtime logs (kv-cache, quant paths) for the canary instances?
DevOps Bot: Logs bundle prepared: s3://redwood-incident-logs/2170003333/canary-1/runtime-logs.tar.gz
Mia (oncall): grabbing logs now. Past 20 minutes I see repeated GC-like stalls on one canary host (host-canary-07).
Sam P.: pinging infra — is host-canary-07 on a different instance type/driver release?
DevOps Bot: host-canary-07 shows kernel driver version nvidia/540.2, all others are 535.x.
Lia Chen: aha — driver mismatch could change kernel scheduling for CUDA kernels. Any recent rollout that could have put model onto that host?
Mia (oncall): yes — autoscaler put canary pods onto spill hosts after load shifted. That host is in the spill pool with older driver.
AJ Rao: hypothesis A — driver mismatch causing slower kernel launches for quantized matmuls, leading to tail latencies. Hypothesis B — new model variant introduced a different KV cache path that causes cold cache regeneration on some workloads.
Mia (oncall): collecting evidence for A & B. Dropping relevant log snippets below.
Mia (oncall): runtime stderr from host-canary-07 (snippet):
```
[2026-03-15T09:12:03Z] INFO kv_cache: miss for prefix 0x7f3a... rebuild start
[2026-03-15T09:12:03Z] WARN cuda: kernel launch slow (elapsed=0.189s) kernel=matmul_fp8
[2026-03-15T09:12:03Z] INFO inference: token generation took 0.42s (partial)
[2026-03-15T09:12:04Z] WARN cuda: kernel launch slow (elapsed=0.57s) kernel=attention
[2026-03-15T09:12:04Z] INFO inference: final token latency 3.14s
```
Mia (oncall): comparing to host-canary-03 (normal host):
```
[2026-03-15T09:12:03Z] INFO kv_cache: miss for prefix 0x7f3a... rebuild start
[2026-03-15T09:12:03Z] INFO cuda: kernel launch elapsed=0.0032s kernel=matmul_fp8
[2026-03-15T09:12:03Z] INFO inference: token generation took 0.11s
```
Sam P.: pretty convincing for driver-related kernel launch slowness. DevOps — can we cordon host-canary-07 from canary pool?
DevOps Bot: marked host-canary-07 unschedulable for canary today. New canary pods draining.
Lia Chen: while draining, do we want a rollback of the model canary? What's the customer impact?
Kate L - PM: Customer impact -> early signal: ~3% of requests to hosted endpoint using this canary saw elevated latency. A/B customers on the canary reported minor UX jank (streaming lag), no errors. Support ticket volume: 4 customers, non-critical. Recommend containment first (drain/cordon) then consider rollback if drift persists.
AJ Rao: can we diff the canary commit (model binary + runtime config) vs pinned prod? I want to ensure it's not a code regression too.
Mia (oncall): attaching canary commit and prod commit diffs.
Mia (oncall): git diff --name-status v2.1.3..canary-2026-03-15
```
M  models/redwood-1/config.json
M  runtime/engine/quant-paths.py
A  runtime/engine/kv-cache-optim.py
```
Sam P.: runtime/engine/quant-paths.py changed to prefer an fp8-fused matmul kernel when available. If the driver doesn't have the optimized kernel, fallback uses slower path — could explain kernel launch slow warnings.
Lia Chen: that aligns with driver mismatch hypothesis. kv-cache-optim was added, could interact too.
AJ Rao: mitigation options: 1) Drain offending host (done). 2) Disable canary routing quickly (stop sending new traffic to canary). 3) Rollback model to v2.1.3 (pin). 4) Force canary only onto homogeneous hosts with proper drivers.
Mia (oncall): I'm pushing a temporary routing change to stop new canary traffic. Will monitor.
DevOps Bot: traffic-switch: POST /infra/route/update {"route":"canary","weight":0} — success.
Mia (oncall): after switch, 95th latency declines to 1.05s in 6 minutes. Trending back to baseline.
Kate L - PM: Good containment. Given limited customer impact, prefer targeted remediation (pin hosts/drivers + improve scheduler) vs immediate rollback. But we need a decision on pin/version to remove canary from rollout pipeline.
Sam P.: for safety let's pin production routing to v2.1.3 for the next 24h while infra fixes the driver scheduling. If that pin is cheap, do it.
AJ Rao: agree. I'll run the pin and create a short task to enforce driver versions in canary spill pool.
Mia (oncall): running model pin command now:
```
# Pin production model to prior version
infractl model pin --model redwood-1 --version v2.1.3 --reason "canary tail latency on mixed-driver hosts"
```
DevOps Bot: infractl: applied pin. Production & hosted traffic pinned to v2.1.3.
Lia Chen: note for RCA — root cause appears to be a combination of (A) autoscaler placing canary pods on a spill host with older GPU driver which increases kernel launch latencies for the new fused kernels, and (B) the canary changed kernel preference (fp8-fused matmul) exposing that driver sensitivity.
Sam P.: next steps (action items):
- AJ: enforce driver-version constraint for canary placement + add scheduler rule.
- Infra: roll update host-canary-07 driver to 535.x and requalify.
- Runtime: add graceful fallback metric when fused kernel is missing (emit metric kernel_fallback=true).
- Product: communicate to CS customers who reported jank; summary email.
Mia (oncall): creating timeline artifact and attaching logs bundle to the incident ticket.
Mia (oncall): timeline:
- 09:10Z canary rollout begins (traffic ramped to 5%)
- 09:12Z latency tail emerges, host-canary-07 logs show slow kernel launches
- 09:15Z pager triggered (95th > SLO)
- 09:18Z host-canary-07 identified, cordoned
- 09:22Z canary traffic stopped, 95th returns near baseline by 09:28Z
- 09:30Z model pinned to v2.1.3
AJ Rao: added tasks: infra#4021 (scheduler driver constraint), runtime#4153 (kernel_fallback metric), ops#4077 (driver patch & requalification).
Kate L - PM: I'll draft a short post-incident note for customers and ops summary. No escalation to execs required.
Sam P.: thanks team — assign back to infra + runtime for RCA follow-ups. I'll close this channel after the postmortem doc is created. :thumbsup:
DevOps Bot: incident ticket updated: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2170003
Mia (oncall): handing off to AJ/Runtime for RCA. Oncall clear at 09:45Z.
AJ Rao: acknowledged — taking ownership for action items.
Lia Chen: adding a final note: we should include the driver mismatch test in our canary checklist (driver matrix + scheduler guards).
Kate L - PM: agree. Closing coordination thread.
